title: Naturality of the specified injective-resolution computation
statement: Let B be abelian with enough injectives, C abelian, both with derived categories, and G:B to C additive. Given specified quasi-isomorphisms a:K to I and b:L to J between bounded-below complexes with injective terms in I,J, and a commuting square a g = f b, the normalized derived-object comparisons RG QK to Q(GI) and RG QL to Q(GJ) commute with f and Gg, already before taking cohomology. Their cohomology comparisons have the same naturality. For a whole indexing diagram of specified resolutions the derived-object comparisons assemble into a natural isomorphism of diagrams. A square of quasi-isomorphisms induces a quasi-isomorphism on actual mapping cones. Cones of bounded-below termwise injective complexes are again bounded below and termwise injective. The cone functor sends any diagram of augmentation squares to a diagram of specified cone resolutions, and the same natural comparison computes all its derived interval images. The comparison is constructed by mapping the specified augmentation and then inverting the derived-functor unit on injectives; it is not an arbitrary cohomology isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply naturality of the right-derived-functor unit to a map of bounded-below injective complexes and invert its components, which are isomorphisms. Apply cohomology and the natural derived/homotopy/complex homology comparison isomorphisms.

A specified quasi-isomorphism becomes invertible under Q. Define the derived-object resolution comparison by the image of its augmentation under RG followed by the inverse-unit comparison. Apply cohomology and the natural derived/homotopy/complex comparisons for the cohomology version. Functoriality sends the augmentation square to a commuting square; compose with the proved inverse-unit naturality square.

Localize the mapping-cone triangle map of a commuting augmentation square. The first two components are invertible, hence the third component is invertible by the five lemma for distinguished triangles. Localization reflects quasi-isomorphisms. A cone vanishes below the smaller of the shifted source bound and target bound, and each of its terms is a biproduct of injectives.

Actual cone maps satisfy identity and composition and hence form a functor on arrows of bounded-below cochain complexes. Whisker the diagram of augmentation squares with this functor. Its components are the proved cone quasi-isomorphisms into termwise injective complexes. Apply the proved whole-diagram normalized resolution comparison to obtain the natural isomorphism for interval cones.

theorem rightDerivedFunctorPlusResolutionIso_naturality
    {K L I J : CochainComplex.Plus B} (a : K ⟶ I) (b : L ⟶ J)
    [QuasiIso a.hom] [QuasiIso b.hom]
    [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I.obj.X n)] [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (J.obj.X n)]
    (f : K ⟶ L) (g : I ⟶ J) (h : a ≫ g = f ≫ b) :
    G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map (DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.map f) ≫
        (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusResolutionIso b).hom =
      (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusResolutionIso a).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.map
          (G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.map ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).map g))
